'''Adolf Weiler''' (1851–1916) was a Swiss [[mathematician]].

== Life and work ==
After his studies in the Department of Mathematics Teachers of the [[ETH Zürich|Polytechnicum of Zurich]], he went to study at [[university of Göttingen]] and [[university of Erlangen]] under [[Alfred Clebsch]] and [[Felix Klein]]. He was awarded doctor in 1874 with a dissertation on quadratic line complexes.{{sfn | Rowe | 2016 | pp=245–246 }} Some years before, in 1872, he constructed a model of the Clebsch's diagonal surface.{{sfn | Hernández | Perea | Polo Blanco | Ramírez | 2006 | p=310 }}

Returned to Switzerland, he was mathematics professor at ''Ryffel Institute'' and he obtained the ''venia legendi'' both at Polytechnicum as the [[University of Zurich]]. His main research was in algebraic geometry.<ref>{{smallcaps|O'Connor & Robertson}}, MacTutor History of Mathematics.</ref>
